mappings.note: What modern planners can take from the Arthashastra - graded road widths and penalties for vandalism. CG-SST2 for the ancient source, C-SST4.2 for the public works being managed.
Kautilya's penalties for damaging waterworks, reservoir dams and paths to public forests and water. Goal-level CG-SST2 for the text; the conservation angle is secondary to what the source says.
Railways generating indirect work - station catering, vending stalls, taxis. CG-SST4 for employment in the economy, LO-137 because the examples are all small trading around a station.
Infrastructure as the engine of development - connecting producers to markets, boosting trade, tourism and security. CG-SST4 for the economic argument, C-SST4.2 for the public works making it.
Dhola Sadiya cutting four hours off the journey and giving year-round access to markets and emergency care. C-SST4.2 for the public work, LO-121 for the flood conditions it was built against.
Khasi and Jaintia root bridges growing stronger over decades without harming the ecosystem. LO-123 for the conservation ethic, C-SST4.2 for the crossing itself.
The railways' dual effect - built for extraction, but unintentionally creating markets and linking settlements. CG-SST2 for the colonial history, C-SST4.2 for the network's lasting economic role.
Full electrification cutting emissions and running costs. LO-122 for the emissions, LO-123 for the energy conservation.
Metros in 23 cities bypassing congestion and cutting urban air pollution. C-SST4.2 for the public work, LO-122 for the air quality.

Aviation for high-value perishables and for disaster response. LO-121 for the emergency use, C-SST4.2 for the sector as infrastructure. (The stored answer breaks off into a watermark and stray option text; see report.)

This row's stem is a question and its answer run together; the scored content is what its own answer resolves - Dhola Sadiya connecting Assam and Arunachal across the Lohit, against the false claim that it is a solar ferry. C-SST4.2 for the public work. (Merged stem; see report.)
Personal computers entering the communications timeline in the 1970s. Communications infrastructure history, competency-level C-SST4.2.

India's 12 major and 217 minor ports and a 50 percent rise in cargo, against the false claim that shipping is not cheapest for bulk. C-SST4.2 for the ports, CG-SST4 for the trade volumes. (Stem survives only as its last line; see report.)
1994 and the arrival of the Internet and World Wide Web on the communications timeline. Competency-level C-SST4.2.
Case study on Satish: a new state highway, a mobile phone for prices, cold storage for the tomatoes. C-SST4.2 for the road and cold chain, LO-137 because part (b) turns on him reading the market.
Case study on Delhi's metro cutting car traffic, running on electricity, with solar-powered stations. LO-122 for the pollution reduced, LO-123 for the renewable power that makes it sustainable.
Case study on an earthquake cutting road access and aircraft carrying vaccines and rescue teams. LO-121 is a direct fit - action in the event of a disaster - so the C-SST4.2 fallback is not needed.
Case study on Rani applying for a scholarship through DigiLocker instead of queueing at the district office. LO-138 exactly - how a citizen deals with a government office, here online.
Case study on a vandalised community park, its cost to residents, and the ancient text that prescribed fines. C-SST4.2 for the social infrastructure, CG-SST2 for part (c) on the Arthashastra.
